newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firms as foreigners buy Polish T-bills.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firms as foreigners buy Polish T-bills.

text.p: The zloty closed just up against the basekt of currencies as foreign investors bought long-term Polish T-bills following the Finance Minister's late Wednesday statement hinting at a cut in the zloty devaluation factor.

Grzegorz Kolodko said the zloty would appreciate by 4.3 percent next year, which dealers said would likely entail a cut in the zloty devaluation factor, now at one percent per month, and stirred up foreign interest in Polish treasuries.
"The zloty inched up today as foreign investors bought significant amounts of Polish T-bills after the Kolodko statement," said Malgorzata Sawicka of Bank Handlowy SA.
The zloty was at 2.7845/60 per dollar, down from 2.7832/42 on Wednesday and at 1.8407/15 to the mark, up from 1.8420/35.
It was at 1.65/1.61 percent from the trading band centre, up from Wednesday's close at 1.61/1.55 percent from parity.

Dealers said the situation on the forex market, recently dominated by importers, reversed during the session when currencies flooded market as foreign investors purchased an estimated 40-60 million of Polish T-bills.
Some dealers said however, that several foreign investors sold paper from their portfolio on Thursday to take advantage of the zloty's intraday gains.
Dealers were mixed on whether foreign T-bill purchases would countinue to push the zloty higher on Friday.
On the money market one-day rates inched up 0.6 point at offer to 19.70/20.0 percent as the market tighted further when the central bank sold 825 million zlotys of its NBP-bills.
At the sale, minimum prices of both the 182-day and 273-day bills, available only for Polish banks, held flat and the average yields were 19.78 and 19.90 percent respectively.
